assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi showed with granular data that household leverage and mortgage credit expansions drive housing booms, consumption collapses and deep recessions. This changed how macroeconomists and policymakers understand the Great Recession and credit cycles. The work links micro evidence to macro outcomes and has had large policy and academic influence.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is the Mian-Sufi program (House of Debt, and the QJE, Econometrica and AER papers on household balance sheets, credit supply and the 2007-09 downturn). Campbell's household finance and mortgage work is valuable but is a distinct contribution, so I would not name him.
assessment.maturity: The main results date from roughly 2009-2017 and have been replicated and extended across countries and episodes. The 2022 prize for banks and financial crises (Bernanke, Diamond, Dybvig) did not cover the household-debt channel. The timing is ripe.
uncertainties: Some debate remains over the relative importance of credit supply versus other drivers of the housing boom.
The committee may view the topic as adjacent to the 2022 prize.
Whether the three-name credit set is the right one.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reshaped understanding of how technology (the task framework, skill-biased change and polarization) and import competition (the China shock) alter labor demand, wages and local labor markets. The influence on research and on trade and technology policy is very large, and it bridges labor, trade and macro.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure for tasks and polarization and for the China shock. Hanson co-leads the trade-shock strand, and Katz anchors the skills-and-technology literature. Dorn is a significant co-author on the China shock, so the three-name limit forces a hard choice and attribution is somewhat contestable.
assessment.maturity: The core papers run from about 2003 to 2016 and have been extensively replicated and refined. Some of the original China-shock magnitudes have been revisited. The body of work is mature and still active.
uncertainties: Attribution between Katz and Dorn within a three-name cap.
Ongoing debate on the magnitude and persistence of the China shock.
Possible overlap with the 2021 and 2025 prize themes on labor and technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-firm trade theory transformed trade analysis by explaining exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and the gains from trade through firm productivity differences. It connects directly to firm-level microdata and to growth and productivity research, and it underpins much of the modern empirical trade literature.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the foundational model. Helpman brought a broader theoretical program (monopolistic competition, trade with heterogeneous firms, and later labor-market frictions). Redding is a leading contributor on quantitative and spatial extensions but is a more recent figure, so I would not name him.
assessment.maturity: The framework dates from the early 2000s and has had two decades of empirical confirmation and extension. Krugman's 2008 prize covered the earlier new trade theory, and the firm-heterogeneity generation has not yet been recognized.
uncertainties: Whether Bernard, Eaton, Kortum and others also deserve credit for the firm-level facts and the Ricardian framework.
Quantification of welfare gains is debated, since the gains from selection depend on the distributional assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and credit cycles (Kiyotaki-Moore) and the financial accelerator (Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist) are the standard way to model how balance-sheet frictions amplify and propagate shocks. They are foundational in modern macro-finance and central-bank modeling.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is a clear two-person core. Gertler's contributions (financial accelerator, and later banking and unconventional policy models with Kiyotaki and Karadi) are central, but he also appears in the New Keynesian candidate. Bernanke's share of the accelerator already went to him in 2022, and Gilchrist is a significant co-author. This complicates the attribution.
assessment.maturity: The papers date from the 1990s and have been validated by the 2008 crisis and subsequent work. The work is mature and well established.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of Bernanke in 2022 may reduce the committee's appetite for this topic.
Allocation of credit among Gertler, Gilchrist and the original authors.
Empirical identification of the amplification magnitude.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation research (Restuccia-Rogerson, and Hsieh-Klenow) offers a quantitative account of why TFP and income differ so much across countries. It links firm-level microdata to aggregate development outcomes and shaped how economists think about distortions in growth and development.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) is the best-known contribution, and Restuccia-Rogerson (2008) the conceptual companion. Restuccia's agricultural-productivity work is also relevant. Rogerson is not credited in this candidate, which is a notable attribution gap.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from 2008-2009 and has had over a decade of application and critique, including debate on measurement error, markups and the quality of the underlying data. It is mature but has been qualified.
uncertainties: Disclosed conflict: I am a long-time collaborator of Klenow, and I do not adjudicate it. I have discounted my ranking for it.
Measurement concerns about the size of the misallocation gains.
Missing credit for Rogerson in the named set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Obstfeld and Rogoff built the intertemporal framework for open-economy macro (the Redux model, the textbook Foundations of International Macroeconomics) and identified exchange-rate disconnect puzzles. The contribution is a very influential synthesis, though it is sometimes more integrative than a single discovery.
assessment.attribution: The Obstfeld-Rogoff partnership is clear for the Redux model and the six major puzzles. Rogoff also has separate work with Reinhart (a different candidate), and Obstfeld has independent contributions on capital flows and financial globalization.
assessment.maturity: The core work dates from 1995-2001 and has been extended over a quarter century. It is mature, but its empirical status is mixed because the puzzles remain only partly resolved.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the work as a synthesis rather than a discovery.
Overlap of Rogoff's name with the Reinhart-Rogoff candidate.
Unresolved puzzles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design opened a tractable new branch of mechanism and information theory, with applications from regulation to platforms and disclosure. It generated a large theoretical literature and cross-field adoption.
assessment.attribution: Kamenica-Gentzkow (2011) is the founding paper. Bergemann and Morris developed the closely related information-design and robust-predictions approach. Gentzkow is also known for media economics, which is separate. Credit among the four is contested, so I limit it to three names.
assessment.maturity: The founding paper dates from 2011, and the field is still expanding. It has been less tested empirically and is younger than the other top candidates.
uncertainties: Relatively recent origin and limited empirical validation.
Which three of the four should be credited.
Overlap with the earlier prizes for information economics and mechanism design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Chetty and coauthors used population-scale administrative data to measure intergenerational mobility, neighborhood effects and the returns to policy. This sharply changed empirical public and labor economics and the public debate on opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear leader of the research program. Hendren (neighborhood effects, marginal value of public funds) and Friedman (mobility and tax records, teacher value-added) are central co-authors, and Katz is credited elsewhere on the list. The team-based nature of the work makes individual attribution harder.
assessment.maturity: Most key results date from 2014-2022. Replication and long-run follow-up are still developing, and some findings (for example, neighborhood effects) are still being tested. This is somewhat early for a prize.
uncertainties: The work is recent and some results are still being tested.
Attribution is spread across a large team.
Methodological critiques of mobility measurement and causal neighborhood effects.
